blocks.text: Here are the main objectives of functional testing as guided by RECON:

items: Safety verification: Checking whether the device correctly performs its assigned safety functions (e.g. whether the machine stops when the E-STOP button is pressed).
Fault detection: Ensuring that the device detects its own faults and switches to a safe state (known as a fail-safe), even if the safety mechanism itself fails.

Compliance with standards and certification: Confirming that the device meets stringent international safety standards (e.g. ISO 13849, IEC 62061), which is essential for the machine to be approved for use.
Risk minimisation: Identification of hazardous situations and reduction of the risk of accidents during operation.
Production process validation (Factory Acceptance Test – FAT): Ensuring that mass-produced devices operate in accordance with technical specifications.

blocks.text: Here is how we carry out such tests step by step:

items: Step 1: Preparation and documentation. Specification analysis: Review of technical documentation and functional requirements to understand how the device should respond. Definition of test cases: Creating instructions specifying how to test a particular safety function. Ensuring safety: We ensure the machine poses no risk to testers during testing.

Step 2: Functional testing methods. Black Box Testing: Testing the machine by forcing an input (e.g. breaking the safety curtain) and verifying the output response (e.g. stopping the drive) without examining the internal structure. Fault injection: Deliberately introducing faults into the system to check whether the safety mechanisms detect the fault and safely shut down the machine.

Step 3: Examples of test procedures. Emergency stop (E-stop): Press the button whilst the machine is running, and check whether the drive stops immediately and that a restart is not possible without a manual reset. Light curtain/scanner: Interrupting the light beam/detection field whilst the machine is in motion to confirm immediate stoppage. Safety door interlock: Open the guard and check that the machine has been shut down (power/torque cut-off).

Step 4: Documenting results. Reporting: Each test must result in a pass (compliant with standards) or a fail. Documentation: Results are recorded in reports and, in modern systems (e.g. with Safety software), generated automatically.
Step 5: Periodic verification. Functional tests are not one-off. They must be repeated periodically to confirm that the device is in ‘as new’ condition and to detect latent, dangerous faults.
